intro: Conduit is not a manufactured product, so the Oct 1, 2026 rule with its 55 percent test does not apply to it. Galvanized steel rigid metal conduit is an iron or steel product: every manufacturing process, including galvanizing, must be in the United States (23 CFR 635.410(b)). HDPE conduit is a construction material: every manufacturing process, from combining the plastic inputs to the finished conduit, must be in the United States (2 CFR 184.6(a)(2)). The tables list only conduit that a state DOT list flags for Buy America; the CFR table at the bottom quotes the rules.
cfr_checked: 23 CFR 635.410 and 2 CFR part 184, current as of November 12, 2026

rules.applies_to: Galvanized steel rigid metal conduit (iron or steel product)
rules.short: All manufacturing processes, including coating, in the US
rules.text: "if iron or steel products are to be used, all manufacturing processes, including application of a coating, for these materials must occur in the United States. Coating includes all processes which protect or enhance the value of the material to which the coating is applied." Galvanizing is a coating. The statute behind this is 23 U.S.C. 313.

rules.applies_to: What makes conduit an iron or steel product
rules.short: Wholly or predominantly iron or steel
rules.text: (iii): "articles, materials, or supplies that consist wholly or predominantly of iron or steel or a combination of both." (vi): predominantly means "the cost of the iron and steel content exceeds 50 percent of the total cost of all its components."

rules.applies_to: Steel conduit: small amounts of foreign steel
rules.text: The rule does "not prevent a minimal use of foreign iron or steel products, if the cost of such materials used does not exceed one-tenth of one percent (0.1 percent) of the total contract cost or $2,500, whichever is greater", valued as delivered to the project.

rules.applies_to: HDPE conduit, and PVC conduit (construction material)
rules.short: All manufacturing processes from combining the plastic inputs to final form in the US
rules.text: "Plastic and polymer-based products. All manufacturing processes, from initial combination of constituent plastic or polymer-based inputs, or, where applicable, constituent composite materials, until the item is in its final form, occurred in the United States." The requirement itself comes from the Build America, Buy America Act, section 70914 (Pub. L. 117-58).

rules.applies_to: What makes conduit a construction material
rules.text: The listed items include "(ii) Plastic and polymer-based products (including polyvinylchloride, composite building materials, and polymers used in fiber optic cables)". Also: "Minor additions of articles, materials, supplies, or binding agents to a construction material do not change the categorization of the construction material."

rules.short: Smelting or melting through shaping, coating and assembly in the US
rules.text: "Non-ferrous metals. All manufacturing processes, from initial smelting or melting through final shaping, coating, and assembly, occurred in the United States."

rules.short: Classified once, as brought to the work site
rules.text: An item "should only be classified into one" category, "based on its status at the time it is brought to the work site", and "must meet the Buy America Preference for only the single category in which it is classified." 23 CFR 635.410(c)(2) says the same for FHWA.

"If an item is classified as an iron or steel product, an excluded material, or other product category as specified by law or in 2 CFR part 184, then it is not a manufactured product." The Oct 1, 2026 rule (US manufacture plus more than 55 percent domestic components) applies to manufactured products only.
